question: Where do I find a fractional CRO in Irvine?
body:
## Direct Answer
You find a fractional CRO in Irvine through four proven channels: fractional-executive marketplaces (Chief Outsiders, Bench Advise, The Fractional CRO), RevOps and GTM advisory boutiques that staff Orange County, warm referrals from local B2B founders and VCs in the Irvine Spectrum and UCI Beall Applied Innovation orbit, and vetted operator networks on LinkedIn. Start with a written scope and revenue-outcome target, then interview three to five candidates for pattern-match against your stage, motion, and industry rather than title prestige.

Hiring a fractional Chief Revenue Officer in Irvine is less about geography than about fit — most engagements run hybrid, so the person may sit in Newport Beach, Costa Mesa, or remote-first across Southern California. What matters is that they have carried a number in a motion like yours, can operate two to three days a week, and will leave behind a repeatable revenue engine rather than a dependency. This guide walks the sourcing channels, the vetting bar, the cost structure, and the onboarding sequence so you hire signal instead of a slide deck.

## What exactly does a fractional CRO do and when do you actually need one?
A fractional CRO owns the entire revenue function on a part-time, fixed-term basis: sales, marketing alignment, customer success expansion, pricing, forecasting, and the RevOps stack that ties them together. Unlike a full-time hire who costs $300K–$450K in base plus equity and takes months to ramp, a fractional operator plugs in for a defined mandate — usually two to four days a week over six to twelve months — and is measured on pipeline coverage, win rate, net revenue retention, and forecast accuracy. In Irvine's dense B2B SaaS, medical-device, and fintech ecosystem, this model fits companies between roughly $2M and $30M in revenue that have product-market fit but a leaky, founder-dependent go-to-market.

The trigger to hire one is rarely "we need more salespeople." It is usually a structural symptom: the founder is still the top closer, forecasts miss by 30 percent every quarter, marketing and sales blame each other, or a board wants a credible revenue operator before the next raise. A fractional CRO diagnoses which of those is the real constraint, then rebuilds the operating cadence. If your problem is purely more headcount and a working playbook already exists, you may only need a fractional VP of Sales or a RevOps consultant — see the channel map below to route correctly. For a deeper breakdown of the diagnostic, see the framework at https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/qa-fractional-cro-scope.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Revenue is stuck] --> B{What is the real constraint}
  B -->|Founder is only closer| C[Fractional CRO]
  B -->|Playbook exists need reps| D[Fractional VP Sales]
  B -->|Data and forecast broken| E[RevOps consultant]
  B -->|Positioning unclear| F[GTM strategist]
  C --> G[Scope six to twelve months]
  D --> G
  E --> G
  F --> G
  G --> H[Written revenue outcome target]
```

## Where are the actual sourcing channels for Irvine and Orange County?
The strongest channel in Orange County is warm referral, because the B2B community here is tightly networked. Founders inside the Irvine Spectrum, tenants of the UCI Beall Applied Innovation incubator, and portfolio companies of local funds like Okapi Venture Capital and Miramar Ventures trade operator names constantly. Ask three local founders one question — "Who fixed your revenue engine without becoming a permanent cost?" — and you will surface two or three names that come pre-vetted by someone who paid for the result. Local peer groups such as Vistage chapters and the OC chapter of Pavilion (the go-to-market executive community) are dense with fractional operators actively taking engagements.

The second channel is fractional-executive marketplaces and boutiques. Chief Outsiders, Bench Advise, TechCXO, and The Fractional CRO all place revenue leaders into Southern California companies and pre-screen for track record. These firms add a margin but reduce your search risk — they will not send you someone who has never carried a number. The third channel is direct LinkedIn sourcing using precise filters: title history containing "CRO" or "VP Revenue," a stint at a company one stage ahead of yours, and a location radius around Irvine, Newport Beach, and Costa Mesa. Filter for operators who already list "fractional" or "advisor" in their headline — that signals availability without a recruiter markup. Cross-reference candidates against RevOps communities like RevGenius and Wizards of Ops to confirm they are respected by peers, not just self-described experts. The full channel-scoring rubric lives at https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/qa-fractional-exec-sourcing.

Do not over-index on physical proximity. Post-2020, most fractional revenue engagements are hybrid or remote-first, and the best operator for a medical-device sales motion may live in San Diego while the best fit for PLG SaaS is remote in Austin. Weight relevant motion experience above zip code, and reserve the geography filter for cases where in-person board meetings or field-sales ride-alongs are genuinely required.

## How do you vet a fractional CRO so you buy signal not a deck?
Vetting is where most Irvine founders lose money, because a fractional CRO's core skill is selling — including selling themselves. Neutralize that by structuring the evaluation around evidence, not narrative. Ask every candidate for two specific engagements where they inherited a broken number and what the pipeline coverage, win rate, and net revenue retention looked like before and after. Vague answers like "I built a high-performing culture" are a red flag; precise answers like "coverage went from 2.1x to 3.4x and forecast variance dropped under 10 percent in two quarters" are what you are paying for. Then take references off-script — call a founder they worked for and ask what broke after the operator left, because a real fractional CRO builds a system that survives their exit.

The second vetting axis is motion fit. A CRO who scaled a $50-per-seat product-led motion will flounder in a six-figure enterprise deal cycle with procurement and security reviews, and vice versa. Map your motion — average contract value, sales cycle length, buyer, channel — and pressure-test whether their reps and wins match it. The third axis is operating chemistry: they will restructure comp plans, reset the forecast, and occasionally tell the founder to stop closing deals. If the founder cannot take that direction, the engagement fails regardless of pedigree. Run a paid two-week diagnostic before committing to a longer term — a real operator will happily deliver a written revenue audit for a fixed fee, and that artifact tells you more than any interview. The 13-point evaluation gate is detailed at https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/qa-fractional-cro-vetting.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Candidate shortlist] --> B[Evidence check]
  B --> C[Motion fit check]
  C --> D[Reference off script]
  D --> E[Paid two week audit]
  E --> F{Passed all four}
  F -->|Yes| G[Sign six month scope]
  F -->|No| H[Next candidate]
```

## What does a fractional CRO cost in the Irvine market?
Fractional CRO pricing generally follows one of three structures, and you should understand all three before negotiating. The most common is a monthly retainer for a set number of days per week — in the Southern California market this typically runs from a lower band for an early-stage two-day-a-week engagement up to a substantially higher band for a three-to-four-day mandate with a seasoned operator who has taken companies through a successful exit. Retainers give you predictable cost and clear availability. The second structure is a project or diagnostic fee: a fixed price for a defined deliverable like a 90-day revenue turnaround plan or a comp-plan redesign, which is ideal for testing fit before a longer commitment.

The third structure blends a lower retainer with performance upside — a smaller monthly fee plus a bonus tied to pipeline growth, closed revenue, or a successful fundraise. This aligns incentives but requires airtight metric definitions so you are not arguing about attribution later. Whatever the structure, insist on a written scope with a named revenue outcome, a fixed term with a review checkpoint, and a clean exit clause. Avoid open-ended "advisory" arrangements that bill monthly with no measurable target — those quietly become a permanent cost with none of the accountability of a full-time hire. I will not quote specific dollar figures here because rates vary widely by operator seniority, days per week, and whether equity is part of the package; get three written proposals and compare structure and outcome, not just headline price. For a cost-modeling worksheet, see https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/qa-fractional-cro-cost.

The comparison that matters is against the alternative, not against zero. A full-time CRO in Orange County carries a fully loaded cost well into the mid six figures once base, bonus, equity, and benefits are counted, plus a three-to-six-month search and ramp. A fractional operator delivers senior judgment in weeks at a fraction of that annualized cost, and you can scale the engagement up toward full-time or wind it down as the revenue engine stabilizes. Frame the spend as buying a rebuilt, documented revenue system — if the engagement leaves behind an accurate forecast, a working comp plan, and a repeatable playbook, it pays for itself long after the operator rolls off.

## What does a strong onboarding and first 90 days look like?
The first 90 days determine whether the engagement compounds or stalls. In the first two weeks, the fractional CRO should run a revenue audit: pull the CRM data, interview the sales and marketing teams, sit in on live deals, and produce a written diagnosis of the top three constraints. Resist the urge to have them start "driving pipeline" immediately — a good operator earns the right to prescribe by first proving they understand your specific leak. By the end of week two you should have a one-page revenue plan with named owners, a corrected forecast, and a weekly operating cadence.

Weeks three through eight are execution: rebuilding the pipeline stages and exit criteria, resetting the comp plan if it is misaligned, tightening the marketing-to-sales handoff, and instrumenting the RevOps stack so the numbers are trustworthy. The operator should be visibly transferring knowledge to your team, not hoarding it — the goal is a system that runs without them. Weeks nine through twelve are about proof: the forecast should start hitting within a tighter variance band, coverage should improve, and you should have enough signal to decide whether to extend, scale toward a full-time hire, or wind down. Set that review checkpoint in the contract from day one so the decision is data-driven, not emotional. The onboarding checklist and 90-day scorecard template are available at https://pulserevops.com/knowledge/qa-fractional-cro-onboarding.

The single biggest failure mode is the founder who hires an operator and then refuses to let go of the revenue function. If you bring in a fractional CRO, you must actually cede the forecast, the comp decisions, and the deal reviews to them for the term — otherwise you have paid a premium for advice you will not take. Treat the engagement as a real leadership handoff with a defined runway, and the fractional model delivers senior revenue leadership at a fraction of the cost and risk of a permanent hire.

## Related questions
### What is the difference between a fractional CRO and a sales consultant?
A fractional CRO owns and is accountable for the revenue number across sales, marketing, and success, operating as an interim executive. A consultant advises and hands you a plan but does not own execution or carry the number.

### Can a fractional CRO work fully remote for an Irvine company?
Yes. Most engagements are hybrid or remote-first, with occasional in-person board meetings or field ride-alongs. Prioritize motion and stage fit over physical proximity unless in-person field sales is central.

### How long should a fractional CRO engagement last?
Typically six to twelve months with a review checkpoint at 90 days. Long enough to rebuild the revenue engine and prove the forecast, short enough to force accountability and avoid a permanent hidden cost.

### Should an early-stage startup hire a fractional CRO or a VP of Sales?
If the go-to-market strategy and playbook are unproven, a fractional CRO builds the whole engine. If a working playbook exists and you simply need execution and rep management, a fractional or full-time VP of Sales is the cheaper fit.

### How do I measure whether the fractional CRO is working?
Track pipeline coverage, win rate, forecast variance, sales cycle length, and net revenue retention against a baseline set in week one. Improvement in forecast accuracy and coverage within two quarters is the clearest signal.

## FAQ
**How quickly can a fractional CRO start in Irvine?**
Most available operators can begin within one to three weeks, versus a three-to-six-month search for a full-time hire. Marketplaces and warm referrals move fastest because the vetting is partly pre-done.

**Do fractional CROs take equity instead of cash?**
Some blend a reduced retainer with equity or performance upside, especially at early-stage startups. Full cash retainers are more common at revenue-stage companies. Define the split and vesting or bonus triggers in writing.

**What company stage is right for a fractional CRO?**
Generally companies from roughly $2M to $30M in revenue with product-market fit but a founder-dependent or leaky go-to-market. Below that, you may need a fractional VP of Sales; well above it, a full-time CRO usually makes sense.

**Can a fractional CRO help us raise our next round?**
Yes. A credible revenue operator who tightens the forecast, improves unit economics, and tells a clean growth story is often hired specifically to make the company fundable before a Series A or B.

**What should be in the fractional CRO contract?**
A written scope, a named revenue outcome, days per week, a fixed term, a 90-day review checkpoint, clear metric definitions for any performance bonus, IP and confidentiality terms, and a clean exit clause.

**How is a fractional CRO different from an interim CRO?**
An interim CRO is usually full-time and fills a gap until a permanent hire lands. A fractional CRO is part-time by design and stays part-time, delivering senior leadership without the full-time cost or a planned replacement.

**What if the engagement is not working after 30 days?**
This is why you set a 90-day checkpoint and start with a paid two-week audit. If the diagnosis is weak or chemistry fails early, the fixed-term structure and exit clause let you end cleanly without a severance fight.

**Do I still need a RevOps person if I hire a fractional CRO?**
Often yes. The fractional CRO sets strategy and cadence but needs someone to run the CRM, reporting, and stack day to day. Some operators bring a RevOps analyst; otherwise, plan to staff that function separately.
